doc.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Song lists and original compositions
summary: Domber encourages original compositions, though some buyers check song lists.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Is there ever an issue about musicians who would like to include some of their original compositions? And when I think about what makes a person buy a CD it’s got to be partly that they look at the songlist.
I like the artist but I also like six of these nine songs.

You’d be amazed at how many people turn over the CD and look at the songlist at the back and say oh yeah, “Sweet Sue” I have that, as if one version of “Sweet Sue” covers the entire gamut of what that song can convey and express and what an individual musician will do with it in playing. But it’s amazing, yes, the songlist is important to some people. But to really answer your question, no I actually encourage musicians to do their original work because as I said I think the essence of music making is to give free
rein to the musician to present himself the way he would like to be presented. And if original music is part of that presentation, yeah, sure.
